fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. Joshua built it "…just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites." (Joshua 8:31). The text even says he built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses (Joshua 8:31). So this wasn't Joshua winging it like a man with no recipe. He was following the instructions he'd been given.

The elders are there, standing with all Israel in verse 33, but the text never says they asked for the altar. It says Joshua built it "…just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites." (Joshua 8:31). The text also says he built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses (Joshua 8:31). Sometimes the people in the room aren't the people who gave the order.

Bless it is! Moses had commanded it earlier, and the text states the purpose plainly: to bless the people of Israel (Joshua 8:33). Half stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, on both sides of the ark. That's a whole lot of standing for a good cause.

problems.problem: Joshua 1:1 does not say that Moses led Israel before Joshua. The claim needs a reference that supports it.
